title: Contrast and concession: the two faces of silver

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *sin embargo* and *no obstante* from B1 Unit 1, *aunque* from A2 Unit 28 and *a pesar de que* from B1 Unit 32. Together they let you say that silver brought wealth and, at the same time, problems: first the good side, then the contrast.

sections.title: Linking opposite ideas
rows: La corona recibió mucha plata. Sin embargo, tuvo muchas deudas.
*sin embargo*: starts a new sentence, comma after it
Los precios subieron; no obstante, otras causas también fueron importantes.
Aunque España recibía plata, mucha plata salió del país.
*aunque* + indicative: a fact that is true
A pesar de que se producía mucha plata, la mayoría seguía siendo pobre.

items.spanish: La corona recibió mucha plata. Sin embargo, tuvo muchas deudas.
items.english: The crown received a lot of silver. However, it had many debts.

items.spanish: Algunas ciudades crecieron; no obstante, muchos trabajadores vivían en condiciones duras.
items.english: Some cities grew; nevertheless, many workers lived in hard conditions.

items.spanish: Aunque España recibía mucha plata, una parte importante salió del país.
items.english: Although Spain received a lot of silver, an important part left the country.

items.spanish: A pesar de que se producía mucha plata, la mayoría seguía siendo pobre.
items.english: Even though a lot of silver was produced, the majority stayed poor.

sections.content: *Sin embargo* and *no obstante* join two sentences or two halves of a sentence with a comma; *aunque* and *a pesar de que* go before the idea that is conceded. With a real fact, use the indicative after both.
